evidence-grounded.why: The criterion holds: both lines are FAIL, and each one names a concrete wrong build. Line 1's build wraps JSON.parse in a try/catch that returns {}. That meets the line, but src/app.js would then merge {} into DEFAULTS and print "listening on 8080" with no message. That checks out against app.js, where DEFAULTS has port 8080 and the catch prints "bad config". So the user still can't see which file is broken or where. Line 2's build deletes or inverts the existing test "bad JSON throws" (it really expects SyntaxError in test/config.test.js), and npm test then passes with nothing checking the diagnostic. Everything cited is real in the repository: src/config.js, the app.js catch and exit 1, the README text "stops it with `bad config: <message>` and exit 1", and the test file. No PASS lines exist, so the PASS rule doesn't apply.
